stories.title: Germany: Union–SPD crisis talks as SPD threatens to block Pflegereform
facts: Health Minister Carsten Linnemann (CDU) still aimed to bring the Pflege package to the black-red cabinet on Wednesday; SPD leaders threaten to block what Fraktionschef Matthias Miersch called a “reines Kürzungspaket.”

SPD demands: a “gerechter Beitrag” from private Pflegeversicherung (toward solidarity/Bürgerversicherung-style balance) and a “Pflegedeckel” on out-of-pocket Heim costs — Saarland’s Anke Rehlinger floated €1,500.

Linnemann rejected the Pflegedeckel on ARD: discussing it is fine, but “wir würden das Problem nicht lösen”; wants a late-Oct structural commission and “erste Hilfe” now so benefits/Beiträge stay stable.
t-online/dpa (Mon 03:09): coalition crisis talks expected today — Merz spokesman cited “Verhandlungen auf Arbeitsebene”; Linnemann: public coalition fights should stay “hinter verschlossenen Türen.”
Pflegekassen-Spitzenverband (Oliver Blatt): year-end deficit path ~€4.4B; “in wenigen Monaten ist das Geld schlichtweg alle.” Patientenschutz’s Eugen Brysch warned against “apokalyptische Szenarien.”
stories.whyItMatters: After bruising Landtagswahlen, Pflege is the first big Monday stress test of whether Merz’s “ohne Abstriche” reform tempo survives SPD red lines — cabinet Wed is now the near-term clock.

stories.title: Iran/Hormuz: Trump expects talks this week; Tehran won’t soften seven-day plan
facts: RNZ / Axios (Sun): Trump says he expects Iran talks to resume this week after rejecting Tehran’s seven-day truce → reopen Hormuz roadmap; “They overplayed their hand” / “not the deal that I want.”
Axios sources: indirect US–Iran talks could start as early as Monday; Trump still muses about renewed strikes while claiming Washington will win “very soon.”
Iran FM Abbas Araghchi (IRIB/Al Jazeera Mon): conditions unchanged — “we will not back down”; open to “real diplomacy” but ready for an “apocalyptic” / “doomsday” war if attacks resume.
RNZ/IRIB wires: IRGC said Sunday it seized a US submersible drone in Hormuz “for espionage,” now under specialist review; Gulf energy chokepoint remains the leverage point.
US UN ambassador Mike Waltz (NBC): called Iran’s ask (lift blockade/sanctions, frozen assets, just to talk) a “pretty cynical attempt.”
stories.whyItMatters: Overnight moves the weekend rejection into a same-week negotiation window — with Iran still tying Hormuz reopening to broad Middle East ceasefire terms, and a claimed US drone seizure raising the risk of miscalculation.

stories.title: Trump asked Xi if China wanted to buy US weapons, ambassador says
facts: Guardian (Sun): US ambassador to China David Perdue told Fox News Trump asked Xi Jinping during last week’s summit whether China would like to buy US arms — “we sell arms to other people around the world.”
Context: Taiwan still waiting on a ~$14B US arms package Trump previously called a “negotiating chip”; Beijing opposes arms sales to the island.
After the interview, the White House told the NYT there are no plans to sell arms to China; State said US law prohibits arms sales to China and there is “no offer or plan.”
Perdue on CNBC Friday had said Taiwan policy including arms sales was unchanged; Taiwan deputy FM Chen Ming-chi separately warned of a “severe” PLA threat across the Strait.
stories.whyItMatters: An on-record ambassador claim that Trump floated arms sales to Beijing — immediately walked back by White House/State — muddies the already ambiguous Taiwan arms signal after the Xi summit.
